9483-the-story-and-song-of-black-roderic.title: Black Roderick
9483-the-story-and-song-of-black-roderic.creator: Dora Sigerson
9483-the-story-and-song-of-black-roderic.description: A book by Dora Sigerson. of all the flying things he met in his going, one only dared to put pain upon him, and she was a honeybee who stabbed his cheek with her sword. "Would I could slay thee," she cried, "ere thou rob the hive of its honey!"  And of all the creeping things that passed him on his way, only one tried to stay him; she was the bramble who cast her thorn across his path so his steed wellnigh stumbled.

arxiv-2101-04480.title: Text analysis in financial disclosures
arxiv-2101-04480.creator: Sridhar Ravula
arxiv-2101-04480.description: Abstract Financial disclosure analysis and Knowledge extraction is an important financial analysis problem. Prevailing methods depend predominantly on quantitative ratios and techniques, which suffer from limitations like window dressing and past focus. Most of the information in a firm’s financial disclosures is in unstructured text and contains valuable information about its health.

arxiv-2105-01490.title: An improved setting for generalized functions: fine ultrafunctions
arxiv-2105-01490.creator: Vieri Benci
arxiv-2105-01490.description: Abstract Ultrafunctions are a particular class of functions defined on a Non Archimedean field 𝔼 ⊃ ℝ \mathbb{E}\supset\mathbb{R} . They have been introduced and studied in some previous works ( [ 6 ] , [ 9 ] , [ 15 ] ,.., [ 23 ] ).

arxiv-2210-04434.title: Improving Code Review with GitHub Issue Tracking PubID: pubid: IEEE/ACM ASONAM 2022, November 10-13, 2022 http://dx.doi.org/10.1145/XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX 978-1-6654-5661-6/22/$31.00 © 2022 IEEE
arxiv-2210-04434.creator: Abduljaleel Al-Rubaye, Gita Sukthankar
arxiv-2210-04434.description: Abstract Software quality is an important problem for technology companies, since it substantially impacts the efficiency, usefulness, and maintainability of the final product; hence, code review is a must-do activity for software developers. During the code review process, senior engineers monitor other developers’ work to spot possible problems and enforce coding standards.

arxiv-2210-14839.title: Cyclic descents, matchings and Schur-positivity Thanks: Both authors partially supported by the Israel Science Foundation, Grant No. 1970/18.
arxiv-2210-14839.creator: Ron M. Adin, Yuval Roichman
arxiv-2210-14839.description: Abstract . A new descent set statistic on involutions, defined geometrically via their interpretation as matchings, is introduced in this paper, and shown to be equidistributed with the standard one. This concept is then applied to construct explicit cyclic descent extensions on involutions, standard Young tableaux and Motzkin paths. Schur-positivity of the associated quasisymmetric functions follows. 1.

arxiv-2310-09670.title: One loop reduced QED for massive fermions within an innovative formalism
arxiv-2310-09670.creator: Victor Miguel Banda Guzmán, Adnan Bashir, Luis Albino, Dania Rodríguez-Tzintzun
arxiv-2310-09670.description: Abstract We carry out a detailed study of the three-point fermion-photon interaction vertex at one loop order for massive fermions in reduced quantum electrodynamics. This calculation is carried out in arbitrary covariant gauges and space-time dimensions within a recently proposed innovative approach based upon an efficient combination of the first and second order formalisms of quantum electrodynamics.

arxiv-2505-12461.title: Entanglement Request Scheduling in Quantum Networks Using Deep Q-Network
arxiv-2505-12461.creator: Gongyu Ni 1 , Lester Ho 1 , Holger Claussen 1 2 3
arxiv-2505-12461.description: Abstract In this paper, a novel Deep Q-Network ( DQN ) based scheduling method to optimize delay time and fairness among entanglement requests in quantum repeater networks is proposed. The scheduling of requests determines which pairs of end nodes should be entangled during the current time slot, while other pairs are placed in a queue for future slots.

pmc-10749877.creator: Dorottya Őri, Péter Szocsics, Tamás Molnár, Lucie Bankovska Motlova, Olga Kazakova, Sabrina Mörkl, Michael Wallies, Mohamed Abdulhakim, Sylvie Boivin, Krista Bruna, Carolina Cabaços, Elvira Anna Carbone, Elona Dashi, Giovanni Grech, Stjepan Greguras, Iva Ivanovic, Kaloyan Guevara, Selay Kakar, Konst
pmc-10749877.description: SummaryBackgroundMental health-related stigma occurs among the public and professionals alike. The lived experience of mental illness has been linked to less stigmatising attitudes. However, data on psychiatrists and the relationship between stigmatising attitudes and psychotherapeutic activity or case discussion groups remains scarce.

pmc-11372575.title: Frontal lobe closed-lip schizencephaly as an atypical cause of adult-onset seizures
pmc-11372575.creator: Ahmed Hafez Mousa, Imad A.M. Abuanza, Mohammad Al-Olama
pmc-11372575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Schizencephaly arises from irregular neuronal migration leading to clefts development in the cerebral cortex. The condition is often detected in childhood and it is extremely rare to go unnoticed. This case highlights a 45-year-old male with no previous medical history who presented with a seizure for the first time in the emergency department after which an MRI was done and detected schizcenphaly which at this point was the first time for the patient to be diagnosed with this condition.

pmc-11519048.title: The intersection of travel burdens and financial hardship in cancer care: a scoping review
pmc-11519048.creator: Arrianna Marie Planey, Lisa P Spees, Caitlin B Biddell, Austin Waters, Emily P Jones, Hillary K Hecht, Donald Rosenstein, Stephanie B Wheeler
pmc-11519048.description: BackgroundIn addition to greater delays in cancer screening and greater financial hardship, rural-dwelling cancer patients experience greater costs associated with accessing cancer care, including higher cumulative travel costs. This study aimed to identify and synthesize peer-reviewed research on the cumulative and overlapping costs associated with care access and utilization.

pmc-11630602.title: Calibration verification for stochastic agent-based disease spread models
pmc-11630602.creator: Maya Horii, Aidan Gould, Zachary Yun, Jaideep Ray, Cosmin Safta, Tarek Zohdi
pmc-11630602.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Accurate disease spread modeling is crucial for identifying the severity of outbreaks and planning effective mitigation efforts. To be reliable when applied to new outbreaks, model calibration techniques must be robust. However, current methods frequently forgo calibration verification (a stand-alone process evaluating the calibration procedure) and instead use overall model validation (a process comparing calibrated model results to data) to check calibration processes, which may conceal errors in calibration.

pmc-11676730.title: Eating- and Weight-Related Disorders in the Armed Forces
pmc-11676730.creator: Hubertus Himmerich, Davide Gravina, Inga Schalinski, Gerd-Dieter Willmund, Peter Lutz Zimmermann, Johanna Louise Keeler, Janet Treasure, Davide Masi, Renata Risi
pmc-11676730.description: Background/Objectives: Like in the general population, the prevalences of eating- and weight-related health issues in the armed forces are increasing. Relevant medical conditions include the eating disorders (EDs) anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, and avoidant restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID), as well as body dysmorphic disorder, muscle dysmorphia, and the relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) syndrome.

pmc-11691658.title: RECRUITMENT STRATEGIES IN LONG-TERM CARE: NEW AND NOVEL APPROACHES
pmc-11691658.creator: Cathy Maxwell, Judith Tate, Lisa Juckett, Kelley Colopietro, Abbey Kilpatrick, Lorraine Mion, Nilanjan Sarkar
pmc-11691658.description: Older adults residing in long term care (LTC) can benefit from social and behavioral research to improve health outcomes and promote evidence-based practice; however, recruitment is often difficult and time/cost-intensive. Systematic reviews of literature report recruitment barriers, as well as specific recruitment strategies.

pmc-13505414.title: Sustained nitric oxide-releasing aliphatic lubricants: Infusion in polymers for enhanced slippery and antibacterial efficacy
pmc-13505414.creator: Grace H. Nguyen, Mark Garren, Vicente D. Pinon, McKenna Clary, Hitesh Handa, Elizabeth J. Brisbois
pmc-13505414.description: Implanted medical devices frequently trigger infection, thrombosis, and surface fouling, creating a critical need for new surface-based strategies that reduce biological complications without systemic drugs. Typically, patients receive treatment for these complications, with the more invasive treatments inherently carrying a greater risk for infection, thrombosis, and adverse events, especially with blood-contacting medical devices.
